about: A Guide-style short on Confucius reading the I-Ching until the cords of the bamboo strips broke three times (韋編三絕). The user, 2026-10-01: 'i think some hitchhikers shorts would be great ... for 1 and 2 - review and converge with astra then execute'. Same look and voice as guide-wangbi. Draft 1. Draft 2: Astra's revision (docs/research/2026-10-01-codex-guide-cords.md), adopted as is by Opus, so round 1 converged.

voice.name: hitchiker's guide v1
voice.note: the user's designed Guide voice ('love it'); plain, even pace, no emphasis announcing the jokes

narration.text: The I-Ching. A Chinese book about change.
narration.picture: Title THE I-CHING beside a simple book outline.

narration.text: A later historian, Sima Qian, says the philosopher Confucius studied it in old age.
narration.picture: A bearded figure beside the book; label 孔子 CONFUCIUS; small label SIMA QIAN'S ACCOUNT.
narration.say: A later historian, Sih-mah Chyen, says the philosopher Confucius studied it in old age.

narration.text: His copy was bamboo strips tied with leather cords. The cords wore through. Three times.
narration.picture: Strips joined by two cords; a small break-and-repair as a counter goes 1, 2, 3. Label 韋編三絕 THE CORDS BROKE THREE TIMES.

narration.text: His collected sayings record a hope: more study, fewer serious mistakes.
narration.picture: Typed: ANALECTS · COLLECTED SAYINGS · 7.17, then MORE STUDY / FEWER SERIOUS MISTAKES.

narration.text: Tradition credits him with the Ten Wings: explanations probably written later.
narration.picture: Ten numbered tabs beside the book; labels TEN WINGS and AUTHOR: DISPUTED.

narration.text: Six Lines reads it for judgment: what makes sense to do here.
narration.picture: A small figure pauses at a fork in a road; WHAT TO DO HERE.

narration.text: Recommended for: rereading. Not recommended for: your last set of cords.
narration.picture: The two summary rows; a spare pair of cords beside the book.

onScreenChinese: 韋編三絕 the cords broke three times

sources.shiji: 史記·孔子世家: 孔子晚而喜易，序彖、繫、象、說卦、文言。讀易，韋編三絕。曰：「假我數年，若是，我於易則彬彬矣。」 ~/projects/chinese-classics-reference/shiji/text/47-kongzi-shijia.md
sources.analects: 論語 7.17: 子曰：加我數年，五十以學易，可以無大過矣 (give me a few more years, to study the Yi at fifty, and I might be free of great mistakes). Zhu Xi notes 五十 may be a copying error for 卒 (to finish). lunyu-jizhu/text/07-shu-er.md
sources.tenWings: The Ten Wings were traditionally attributed to Confucius (Sima Qian lists him ordering the Tuan, Xici, Xiang, Shuogua, Wenyan); since Ouyang Xiu (11th c.) and in modern scholarship they are held to be later, Warring States to Han.
